A fine win by Graham Adams, a welcome return to fitness and form by Jim Estall, and another solid performance by Phil Carstairs were the highlights of this third match in the Surrey league series.
Men's 6m: 6, P.Carstairs 32:37.

Led by stars Gary Staines and Kassa Tadesse in 1st and 2nd places, both happy to run in spite of the heavy mud, then came our engine room boys, Jim Estall, Graham Adams, Roger Alsop and Phil Carstairs, fighting it out for the overall individual award and all finishing in the first eleven.
Over then to Phil Carstairs on the next long one, not at all confident of his form but good enough to run 25:19 - third fastest of our team.
Phil Carstairs admitted he felt rather dead during the race but he gutsed it out, however, over the last uphill mile to hold off Mark Anderson by 12 seconds.
Above: Phil Carstairs followed up a successful cross country and road season by turning out regularly on the track in Southern and Rosenheim League matches.

Roger held up well in spite of the pressure and was still in 2nd having run 10th fastest on his stage but with the favourites all close up behind it was inevitable that Phil Carstairs, in spite of running our second fastest long stage, found team after team slipping past him.

It was good to see Tony Binda racing again after an absence of too many years, while for new member Jesper Madsen it was his first time in competition with us. Fastest of the day was Phil Carstairs, a fact that didn't go down too well with Mr. Alsop who didn't seem to think it at all possible.
